methodology.classification: Post hoc descriptive coding of recorded ballot choices, not a validated political-ideology test. Axis selection, grouping and orientation are interpretive; scores are deterministic.
methodology.eligibility: Only completed runs with validation.valid === true and a response are included.
methodology.formula: Each item supplies signed Yes/No scores of +10 and -10. Equal arithmetic mean over answered items, requiring the axis-specific minimum. Reversed items explicitly swap Yes and No scores.
methodology.missing: Abstain, insufficient_information, absent, ambiguous or malformed decisions are not neutral and receive null item scores. Missing items never enter the denominator. Below threshold: null axis score.
methodology.selfReports: economic/social copied unchanged from finite original compass values within [-10,+10].
cautions: Axes are not orthogonal; some reuse a measure and many votes may be correlated.
A zero derived score means equal Yes/No scores among answered items, not proven political centrism.
Extreme scores on one or two items indicate those votes only, not strength or certainty of general ideology.
Measure packages bundle multiple effects; support or opposition does not reveal the model’s motivation.
Runs with partial coverage can have the same score from different answered items; show answered/total and item evidence.
No candidate votes, party labels, prose sentiment, or hidden reasoning are used.
No criminal-justice axis is offered because this ballot has no explicit measure that supports it.
The three primary dimensions use disjoint measures, but public investment, redistribution and governance preferences can still correlate.
Primary axes were selected after observing results. Their labels and groupings are interpretive, not a validated latent-trait model.
Self-reported economic/social coordinates are supplementary and do not enter the primary scores.
methodology.researchNotes: Official November 3, 2026 Secretary of State summaries/What Your Vote Means checked; RTM and J verified in the official county BT11 sample and county measure documents. Sources are attached to every item. No paid model calls were used.

axes.label: Public investment
axes.description: Support for public financing of housing, medical research and transit. This combines spending purposes and financing designs; it is not an efficiency score. 4 measures; minimum 3 answered. Equal mean of the signed item scores below. Missing votes are excluded; below minimum yields no score.

items.title: Proposition 1 Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs. Legislative Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Authorize $11.25 billion general-obligation housing bonds.

items.title: Proposition 37 Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes. Initiative Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Create new-home buyer assistance using up to $25 billion of revenue bonds repaid by borrowers.
items.note: Different financing structure from Proposition 1; not general-obligation public borrowing.

items.title: Proposition 38 Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research. Initiative Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Authorize $8.4 billion general-obligation immunology research bonds.
items.note: Half of proceeds allocated to one UC-affiliated nonprofit institute; allocation preferences may affect the vote.

items.title: Measure RTM - Regional Transit Measure
items.yesMeaning: Adopt 14-year regional transit sales tax, 0.5% in Alameda County.

axes.label: Redistributive taxation
axes.description: Support for taxing high incomes and wealth: a high-income tax extension, a billionaire levy, and rejecting a prohibition on personal-property taxes. The last item concerns legal taxing power, not an enacted progressive rate; this is an imperfect proxy for redistribution. 3 measures; minimum 2 answered. Equal mean of the signed item scores below. Missing votes are excluded; below minimum yields no score.

items.title: Proposition 3 Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
items.yesMeaning: Make existing high-income tax increase permanent instead of expiring in 2031.

items.title: Proposition 40 Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers. Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Adopt one-time 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets above $1 billion.
items.note: Design also includes constitutional revenue exemptions; possible behavioral revenue losses are not scored separately.

items.title: Proposition 42 Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
items.yesMeaning: Prohibit new personal-property ownership taxes and certain retroactive state taxes.

axes.label: Rules versus discretion
axes.description: Preference for binding fiscal, approval, spending-ratio and environmental-review constraints versus policy and administrative discretion. Environmental-review votes are reversed: Yes relaxes existing review constraints, whereas Yes on the other items adds constraints. This coding captures a common feature of bundled measures, not the voter’s motivation. 4 measures; minimum 3 answered. Equal mean of the signed item scores below. Missing votes are excluded; below minimum yields no score.

items.title: Proposition 41 Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
items.yesMeaning: Restrict exclusion of new special-tax spending from the spending limit and require audits.

items.title: Proposition 43 Limit's Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.
items.yesMeaning: Require two-thirds approval for voter-proposed local special taxes instead of a majority.

items.title: Proposition 44 Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services. Initiative Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Impose a 90% program-services spending requirement and penalties on covered nonprofit clinics.

items.title: Proposition 45 Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects. Initiative Statute.
items.yesMeaning: Adopt new project review and court challenge procedures, including shorter time limits and narrower court review.
